sources.name: PS5 Remote Play
sources.controls: Your controller connects to this PC; chiaki-ng sends it to the PS5
sources.guide: Connect your PS5 with chiaki-ng (SmoovPlay sets it up), then press Play.

sources.name: Capture card
sources.audio: SmoovPlay plays the card's sound, in step with the picture
sources.controls: Your controller connects to the console as usual
sources.guide: Connect the console's HDMI to the capture card and the card to this PC. On a PS5, turn off HDCP while you use it (Settings > System > HDMI). Set the console to 1080p, 60 Hz, HDR off (or the Capture card resolution picked in Settings).

sources.name: App window
sources.audio: The app plays its own sound, a little ahead of the picture
sources.controls: Your controller connects to the app as usual
sources.guide: Open the app you stream with (PS Remote Play, the Xbox app, Moonlight, or a browser) and start the game, pick its window, then press Play. Keep the app's window on screen: SmoovPlay shows the smooth picture on top of it, and the app keeps the controller and the keyboard. SmoovPlay's own keys use Ctrl+Alt (Ctrl+Alt+M menu, Ctrl+Alt+F fullscreen, Ctrl+Alt+Esc quit), and can be changed on the Play page.

sources.name: Frame tap (for developers)
sources.audio: The app plays its own sound
sources.controls: Your controller connects to the app as usual
sources.guide: For app developers: an app built to send its frames straight to SmoovPlay (docs/frame-tap.md in SmoovPlay's repo). For the Xbox app, PS Remote Play, Moonlight or a browser, pick App window instead. Press Play, then start the app: its smooth video opens in its own window, and the app keeps the controller and its sound.

sources.name: Video file
sources.guide: For testing: a video file played as a source.
